Fact necessary to dispose of this Rule, In brief, is that preemptor-opposite-party instituted pre-emption Case No.7 of 1993 in the Court of the Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla, seeking pre-emption of the land schedule No.1. In that pre-emption petition she alleged that land of schedule-1 originally belonged to (1) Chand Gazi, (2) Hosenuddin and (3) Shamsher Ali. Chand Gazi died leaving only son Yeas in and Yeasin died leaving five daughters-Pre-emptor and opposite party Nos.6 to 9 and two sons-opposite-party Nos.4 and 5. He had another daughter named Mirjan who died during his lifetime. Shamser Ali died leaving heirs opposite- party Nos. 10 to 13 and Hosenuddin died leaving one son named Nawab Ali-opposite-party No.3. In the pre-emption application, preemptor-petitioner alleged that she is not only a co-sharer by inheritance but also a co-sharer by purchase, as she purchased some land from Sayedunnessa and Obaidul Hoque by two registered deed Nos. 164 and 171 dated 6-2-1991. That the opposite-parties Nos. 14 to 25 are co-sharers by purchase and opposite-party No.3 without issuing any notice upon the pre-emptor-petitioner sold the case land to pre-emptee-opposite-party No.1 at a consideration of Taka 1,50,000 by the registered deed dated 4-12-1995. Pre-emptor- petitioner had no knowledge of this transfer. She came to know of the transfer on 6-12-1995 and after taking certified copy on 7-12-1995 has filed this pre- emption case. 

 6. We have perused the impugned judgment and order of both the Courts below together with the miscellaneous application and written-objection and the exhibited documents filed by the parties in this miscellaneous case. It is found that by Exhibit Ka a separate Khatian has been prepared in the name of Nawab Ali at a Jama of Taka 9 in Mutation Case No.717 of 1979-80. That Khatian was approved by the then Circle Officer (Revenue), Barura, on 15-4- 1980 and since then Nawab Ali is paying rents as per his separate Khatian. Now, what would be the implication of this mutation case in the original Khatian and holding? In the case of Fatema Bibi vs Manik Lal Samaddar and others their Lordships of the Appellate Division held that when the Khatians are different, the pre-emptor cannot be held to be a co-sharer in the case holding and not entitled to pre- emption. This decision of the Hon'ble Appellate Division was given in a case filed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.
